topics.title: Rotation
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Identify the order of rotational symmetry of plane figures. (k, u, s)
Distinguish between clockwise and anti-clockwise rotation. (k, u)
State properties of rotation as a transformation including congruence. (k, u)
Determine the centre and angle of rotation. (u, s)
Apply properties of rotation in the Cartesian plane. (u, s, v/a)

body.text: The order of rotational symmetry of a shape is the number of times it looks exactly the same during one full 360° turn. An equilateral triangle has order 3 (it matches its original outline every 120°); a square has order 4; a shape with no repeat until the full 360° turn has order 1 (no rotational symmetry).

A rotation is described completely by three things: the centre of rotation (the fixed point everything turns around), the angle of rotation, and the direction (clockwise or anti-clockwise). Rotation is a congruent transformation — the image is exactly the same size and shape as the object, just turned.
Rotate the point (3, 1) by 90° anti-clockwise about the origin (0, 0). The rule for a 90° anti-clockwise rotation about the origin is (x, y) -> (-y, x). Applying it: (3, 1) -> (-1, 3).

To find the centre of rotation between an object and its image, join a point on the object to its matching point on the image, construct the perpendicular bisector of that line, and repeat for a second pair of points — the two perpendicular bisectors cross at the centre of rotation.
